items.title: Modification of arbitral awards: Not the need of the hour
items.summary: A recent column here made the case for a legislative amendment in the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 to provide courts with the power to modify awards in domestic arbitration. The column, in its conclusion, suggests that the scope of this amendment will be “ restricted to domestic India-seated awards falling foul of public policy ”. This essay is a response to the column and argues that India’s arbitration ecosystem requires a return to the basics, rather than reforms to appease the naysayers. Gayatri Balaswamy and its aftermath In the original column, the author covers the aftermath of the Supreme Court’s decision in Gayatri Balaswamy and how its unruly categories for when the power to modify is appropriate have led to more chaos than calm. Interestingly, the column makes the case for why the Supreme Court’s ability to modify the award under Article 142 will have "terrible consequences as a party will ultimately never be certain as to what the ultimate outcome will be (and whether an award will be modified eventually) (…) Businesses rely on certainty and predictability, and are loathe the use of unbridled discretion... ” I agree with this wholeheartedly. One of the bedrock principles of arbitration is finality: parties consciously choose to resolve their disputes through arbitration instead of traditional court-based litigation for its bespoke advantages of autonomy, efficiency and finality. Justice Viswanathan’s dissent focused on these principles when he explained how modification would cut against the core idea of minimal judicial interference in Section 5 of the Arbitration Act. He also explained why the majority’s decision would disturb the legislative scheme for setting aside of arbitral awards – which made no mention of a power to modify or vary the award. Specifically, in the context of Article 142, it is even more troubling. If the Supreme Court wields the power to modify awards at a discretionary last stage of judicial proceedings (an SLP, after all, is a discretionary power sparingly exercised), parties lose one of arbitration’s core advantages and uncertainty looms. But if it is understood that modification takes away the advantage of finality and diminishes predictability for parties, why propose entrenching it through legislation instead? items.title: Builder's RERA violations cannot make lenders criminally liable: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently held that violation of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA) by builders of a project cannot, by itself, form the basis for criminal prosecution of lenders who had extended loan facility to the builders for the concerned project [ Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Company Limited v. State of NCT of Delhi & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta observed that the obligations under the relevant RERA provisions are primarily those of the promoter. "Alleged contraventions of RERA ... by themselves neither give rise to nor can they sustain prosecution for offences under the IPC. In particular, they cannot be made the foundation of a prosecution of a lender who is not the regulated entity, in the absence of the specific ingredients of the offence/s defined in IPC," the November 18 judgment stated. The Court also clarified that its earlier directions for preliminary enquiries by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into the builder-bank nexus in the National Capital Region (NCR) does not mean that lenders could be prosecuted merely because a developer had defaulted. "Nothing in those orders lays down that every lender to a real estate developer is, by reason of the developer’s default, exposed to criminal prosecution at the instance of any party aggrieved against the developer," the Court observed. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The Court explained that the obligations under the relevant provisions of RERA were those of the promoter and that the Act provides its own regulatory mechanism for enforcement. The observations came while quashing criminal proceedings against L&T Finance Limited and Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (EARC) in a dispute involving Raheja Developers Limited. The case arose from a collaboration agreement between Raheja Developers and certain landowners for developing a housing project in Gurugram. In 2016, L&T sanctioned a ₹450 crore loan facility to the developer, secured by mortgages over four project lands, including a portion of the landowners' property. The facility was enhanced to ₹620 crore in 2018. Subsequently, the loan account and underlying securities were assigned to EARC in 2019. The landowners alleged that the loan facility was enhanced without their consent and that project receivables were used to repay the loan instead of paying their agreed revenue share, in violation of their contractual rights and RERA provisions. items.title: Bank of Baroda assures Bombay High Court it will preserve records in BR Shetty's $15B fraud suit
items.summary: Bank of Baroda on Thursday assured the Bombay High Court that it will preserve all the documents sought by NMC Health founder Dr. Bavaguthu Raghuram Shetty in connection with his $15 billion damages suit against the public sector lender [ Dr BR Shetty v. Bank of Baroda & Ors.] Justice Arif S Doctor recorded the undertaking given by Senior Advocate Birendra Saraf appearing for the bank, after Shetty’s counsel pressed for interim protection of the records. “He, however, assures the Court that all such documents forming part of the Schedule to the Interim Application and in the custody or control of Defendant No. 1 shall be preserved as they are. His statement is accepted,” the Court recorded on November 19. Justice Arif Doctor Shetty in his suit has alleged fraud, collusion, negligence, and reputational loss by the bank and former NMC executives Prasanth and Promoth Manghat. The suit claims Bank of Baroda closed anti-money-laundering alerts without inquiry and facilitated round-tripping after he stepped down as CEO in March 2017. Through his interim applications, he has sought forensic imaging of the bank's electronic systems, discovery on oath from the bank and ten officers, suspension of deletion policies, and $15 billion (around ₹1,43,700 crore) in security or balance-sheet provisioning. The matter will next be heard on December 17. During the hearing on Thursday, Shetty’s counsel, Senior Advocate Zal Andhyarujina sought ad-interim disclosure of documents listed in the schedules to the interim application. He argued that if the Court was not inclined to grant disclosure at present stage, the bank could be directed to preserve the records so they are not tampered with. Senior advocate Zal Andhyarujina Saraf opposed the relief contending that the documents already form part of proceedings before an Abu Dhabi court. He called Shetty’s apprehensions ‘wholly baseless’. He however assured the Court to preserve the records in the bank's control. Senior advocate Birendra Saraf Saraf also informed the Court that the bank had moved an application seeking deferment of the hearing. He referred to the Abu Dhabi court judgment holding Shetty complicit in the very fraud he alleged in his suit. He further argued that the cause of action arose in 2020 and that the suit is barred under Rule 89 of the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) Court of First Instance Court Procedure Rules, 2016. items.title: Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp at Thiruparankundram as one time measure but stays Madras High Court observations
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday allowed the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam as a one-time measure this year at the disputed stone pillar near the Arulmigu Subramania Swamy temple and the Sikandar Badusha Dargah on the Thiruparankundram hillock in Madurai. However, the Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi stayed observations made by the Madras High Court as regards the nature of the pillar and the land on which it stands. Worship at the customary sites and lawful access to the Dargah and mosque must continue undisturbed, the top court made it clear. Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi The lamp can be lit only by a small team from the temple, the size and composition of which has to be decided by the Madurai District Collector in consultation with the temple Executive Officer, ASI and Police Commissioner. The Collector will supervise the arrangements and the police will provide security, with CRPF support if required and feasible, the Court said. "Public gatherings, processions, demonstrations and slogan-raising are barred at the site," the Bench underscored. Access should be limited to the authorised team and officials needed for supervision and security. The district administration will fix the timing, route and duration for lighting the lamp, must leave immediately after the ceremony and should not leave any material behind after the ceremony. The Court also barred excavation, construction and structural alterations at the disputed site. "Neither the permission nor the ceremony can be relied on as proof of custom or a right of access, or as a basis for permission in future years, " the Court further said. In a nutshell - Lighting of lamp permitted as one time measure; - Madras HC findings on the nature of the pillar and the land stayed; - A small team to be decided by Collector can only light the lamp; - Access to the site only for the team and their security; - Public gatherings, processions, slogan-raising barred at the site; - Excavation, construction, structural alterations barred; - Worship at the customary sites and access to Dargah, mosque must continue undisturbed; - Permission to light lamp not proof of any custom or right of access. items.title: AP raises semiconductor incentives, offers up to 80% support for silicon fabs
items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government has amended its Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy 4.0 to align it with the second phase of the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM 2.0), offering state incentives that match Union support for several project categories. The amendment, notified through G.O.Ms.No.87 on November 16, provides combined Union and State incentives of up to 80% of eligible capital costs for silicon fabrication projects, with each government contributing 40%. Compound semiconductor, photonics, sensor, discrete semiconductor and display fabrication projects, as well as advanced packaging units, will be eligible for combined support of up to 70%. Legacy packaging units can receive up to 50%, according to the policy details. For assembly, testing, marking and packaging (ATMP) and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) facilities, Andhra Pradesh will match 100% of the Centre’s capital support. The state will also provide a deployment-linked incentive of 4.5% of net sales, in addition to the Union’s 9%, taking the combined incentive to 13.5%. This support will be capped at Rs 45 crore per application and Rs 180 crore per company. For semiconductor machinery and materials projects, the state will provide 18% of eligible capital costs on top of the Union’s 30%, bringing the combined support to 48%, in addition to the Union’s production-linked incentive. Research and development and talent projects will receive state support of 25% of eligible project costs, with combined Union and State assistance capped at 75%. IT Minister Nara Lokesh said the amended policy covers all 10 categories under ISM 2.0, across six pillars: design, machinery and materials, fabrication, packaging, research and development, and talent. The state is also planning a 5,000-acre AP Semiconductor Park in Tirupati to host manufacturers and suppliers across the value chain. The proposed park would provide developed land, shared cleanrooms, reliable high-voltage power, ultrapure water, gas supplies, effluent treatment and recycling, testing laboratories, logistics facilities, and research and training centres. A public-private company with an investor-led board would operate the park, with up to three government nominees. The government also plans to establish an AP Semiconductor Growth and Innovation Council as a single point of contact for investors, alongside an Oversight Council chaired by the Chief Minister and a CEO-led Apex Committee. items.title: UoH students launch protest seeking professor’s termination over casteist remarks
items.summary: University of Hyderabad students have launched an indefinite protest demanding the termination of Dr Vijaya Ramdas Mandala, a faculty member in the History Department, over his alleged derogatory remarks about Dalit students in an email exchange. The remarks were allegedly made after a former student expressed hesitation regarding incorporating certain suggestions made by Vijaya Ramdas into his research because of ethical concerns. The incident took place in April but came to light only recently. The protest has been called by the Students’ Union, which comprises various student groups, including the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the Ambedkar Students’ Association, the Dalit Students’ Union,and the Tribal Students’ Forum. Students have been staging a sit-in outside the Social Sciences building, demanding Vijaya Ramdas’s termination. “We will not call off the protest until Vijaya Ramdas is terminated,” Students’ Union general secretary Aditya Rao told TNM. “We had protested earlier too, but no concrete action was taken against him,” he added. In an email exchange accessed by TNM, Vijaya Ramdas contacted Sandeep (name changed), who is a PhD student at Manchester Business School, about corrections to his chapter for a forthcoming book by Bloomsbury India. In the email thread, the History professor refers to former students from the Dalit community as “untouchables” more than once. He also refers to another student studying at Nottingham as “Dalit untouchable idiot”. The men’s families and human rights organisations have maintained that these were unprovoked extrajudicial murders. At the time, police said they stumbled on the men attempting to cut down red sanders trees for smuggling. But allegations only grew that the so-called ‘encounter’ was staged. No clear answers have emerged since. Their deaths are the heart of Director Rajkumar Periasamy’s OM: Operation Mole. Dhanush plays Palani alias Thirukumaran, a special operative trained in infiltrating organised crime networks. He’s soon sent undercover to a Red Sanders smuggling operation. Here, Palani meets Karthikeyan (Mammootty), who oversees the Chennai arm of the network. Karthikeyan, like Mammootty in the 1991 Thalapathi , is a gangster well-loved by his neighbourhood. He has his own codes and is mindful of who is most vulnerable to the ongoing feud between smugglers and cops. He values loyalty above all else. As Palani and Karthikeyan grow closer, OM makes some vague attempts to recall the bond between Devaraj (Mammootty) and Surya (Rajinikanth) in Thalapathi but isn’t too serious about it. Palani’s handler is Nithya Reddy (Sai Pallavi), who heads the AP task force. She has personal as well as professional reasons to stop the smuggling network. Muhammed Ameer, an ‘educator’ and one of the prominent faces of the Malayalam digital platform Unmasking Anomalies (UA), had an answer. “Consider”, he said, “the amount of sexual imagery men are exposed to every day, from hoardings and advertisements to models.” A man sees a sexually exposed woman and becomes sexually frustrated. Just as someone who cannot shout back at a boss might take their anger out on someone at home, he argued, sexual frustration can be taken out on a different target. This, Ameer said, was “frustration-aggression theory”. When another panellist objected that this did not explain why women should change what they wear, Ameer was emphatic. “This is a psychological theory,” he asserted. “It’s not me saying this.” It is an effective way to make an argument, enough to make the person sitting across from you in a debate pause and reconsider what they can immediately challenge. items.title: Chennai: 71.24 kg heroin worth Rs 140 crore seized from ice cream vending vehicle
items.summary: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) seized around 71.24 kg of heroin, worth Rs 140 crore, from an ice cream vending vehicle near Madhavaram in Chennai on Tuesday, November 17. Two men have been arrested in connection with the seizure and remanded to judicial custody. The accused have been identified as Abdul Shukkur (32) and his brother-in-law Shafiq Ahmed (30), both natives of southern Tamil Nadu who were residing in Chennai. According to reports, the DRI received specific intelligence inputs on Monday night about a large consignment of narcotics being smuggled from abroad and being transported through vehicles in Chennai suburbs. Following the tip-off, special teams were formed and surveillance was intensified near Chennai airport and along the Chennai-Tiruchy and Chennai-Kolkata National Highways. On Tuesday, DRI officials spotted an ice cream vending vehicle parked near an ice manufacturing factory in Madhavaram, along the Chennai-Kolkata National Highway. The vehicle was reportedly waiting to load ice from the factory. During a search of the vehicle, officials found several packets of heroin stacked inside its freezing unit and hidden among the racks used to store ice cream. The officials subsequently arrested the two men who were inside the vehicle. Officials suspect that an international drug trafficking network had engaged them to move the narcotics using the ice cream vehicle as cover, believing that such a vehicle would be less likely to attract checks from the police and anti-narcotics agencies. The two men were produced before the court in Alandur on November 18 and remanded to judicial custody. Reacting to the seizure, former Chief Minister and Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) president MK Stalin alleged that the deterioration of law and order under the TVK government, along with alleged sexual misconduct by ruling party functionaries, robberies, burglaries and custodial deaths, had turned Tamil Nadu into a “vice city”. “The DGP may say that a case has been registered. But he should explain why the state police have been unable to arrest drug traffickers. What happened to the 65 units formed to prevent drug use and trafficking in the state? Chief Minister Vijay holds the Home portfolio. If he is not prepared to offer an explanation now, when will he do so?” Stalin asked.
